title: How to Calculate Your Annual Pay: Salary Package Meal Entertainment and Casual Loading Explained
description: Learn how to convert your hourly rate to annual salary including casual loading and super. Understand salary package meal entertainment and its impact on your pay.
salarySummary: For a full-time employee working 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. Casual loading of 25% and super of 12% are paid on top.

faqs.q: What is salary package meal entertainment?
faqs.a: Salary package meal entertainment is a fringe benefit where an employer provides meal entertainment (food, drink, and associated travel or accommodation) to an employee. Under Australian Taxation Office rules, if the benefit is not provided through a salary packaging arrangement, it may be excluded from reportable fringe benefits. This means it does not appear on your payment summary and does not affect your base hourly-to-annual calculation, but it can influence your overall remuneration package.

faqs.q: How does casual loading work in the annual pay calculation?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an additional 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate for the lack of paid leave entitlements such as annual leave and sick leave. When using the timesheet tool, you enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box; the tool automatically adds 25%. Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading. The annual estimate then reflects the higher casual rate.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in the annual pay estimate?
faqs.a: No, superannuation is paid on top of your gross pay. The annual pay estimate shows your gross earnings before super. The super guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Your employer must pay this separately, so your total employment cost is higher than the annual figure shown.

bodyMarkdown:
## Converting Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

To estimate your annual gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, we assume 38 hours per week, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. The formula is:

**Annual gross ≈ hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For example, at the National Minimum Wage of $26.44 per hour, working 38 hours a week gives an annual gross of $26.44 × 38 × 52 = $52,245.44. Your fortnightly pay would be roughly $2,009.44 (weekly × 2).

This calculation assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. It is an estimate, not a determination of your actual pay.

## The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. Many employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates, penalties, and allowances. You can find the correct rates for your industry in the [pay guides](/blog) published by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

Award rates often include annualised wage arrangements, where a fixed annual salary covers minimum pay, penalties, overtime, allowances, and annual leave loading. The Fair Work Ombudsman explains that such arrangements must be reviewed every 12 months to ensure the employee receives at least what they would have under the award.

## Casual Loading: 25% on Top

If you are a casual employee, your base hourly rate is increased by 25% casual loading. This compensates for not receiving paid leave such as annual leave, personal leave, and public holidays. When using [the timesheet](/), you enter your base hourly rate and check the casual loading box. The tool adds 25% automatically. **Never enter a rate that already includes casual loading** – the tool does the addition for you.

For example, if your base rate is $30.00 per hour, the casual rate becomes $37.50. Your annual estimate would then be $37.50 × 38 × 52 = $74,100. Your fortnightly pay would be about $2,850.

## Superannuation: Paid on Top of Your Gross

Superannuation is not included in the annual gross figure shown by the calculator. The super guarantee requires your employer to pay an additional 12% of your ordinary earnings into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For a full-time worker on the minimum wage, that means an extra $6,269.45 per year in super. The total employment cost to your employer is your gross pay plus super.

## Salary Package Meal Entertainment: What It Means for Your Pay

Salary packaging allows you to sacrifice part of your pre-tax salary for certain benefits. One common benefit is meal entertainment – food, drink, and associated travel or accommodation provided by your employer. The Australian Taxation Office provides a reporting exclusion for entertainment-related benefits. If the meal entertainment is not provided through a salary packaging arrangement, it may be excluded from reportable fringe benefits. However, if it is part of a salary package, it must be reported and can affect your take-home pay.

The annual pay estimate on this site does not deduct salary sacrifice amounts. If you have a salary package that includes meal entertainment, your actual taxable income will be lower, and your take-home pay may be higher than the estimate suggests. Always consult your employer or a tax professional to understand how packaging affects your situation.

## Using the Timesheet and Pay Guides

The [timesheet](/) on this site lets you enter your base hourly rate, add casual loading, and see your annual, fortnightly, and weekly pay. For accurate award rates, refer to the [pay guides](/blog) from the Fair Work Ombudsman. The [reference tables](/data) provide historical pay rates and the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page has the latest figures.

## Tax and Medicare

Tax is calculated using the 2026–27 resident tax scale: nil on the first $18,200, 15% on income up to $45,000, 30% up to $135,000, 37% up to $190,000, and 45% above that. The Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page shows an estimate after tax and Medicare, but does not include HELP repayments, the Medicare levy surcharge, or salary packaging.

## Conclusion

Converting your hourly rate to annual pay is straightforward: multiply by hours per week and 52. Remember that casual loading and super are paid on top. If you have a salary package that includes meal entertainment, your taxable income may be reduced. Use the tools on this site to get a clear picture of your earnings, and always check the applicable award or agreement for your exact entitlements.
